analysis: Documentation-only PR, no code, workflow or threat-model changes. docs/operations/provider-release.md head lines 21-36 change the 'prepared' version from 0.9.21 to 0.9.22 and describe native Bonsai 9B request/vision/MTP-sidecar support. They record v0.9.21 as published on 2026-10-14. The text says source preparation is not release qualification and that no tag, registration, upload or deployment is performed. It tells the reader to confirm sidecar artifacts, distribution IDs, sampled-MTP correctness, memory/media admission and platform compatibility before promotion. The signing, notarization, R2 staging, registration, rollback and revocation sections are otherwise unchanged. Prerequisites still say the pipeline relies on App Attest qualification, official CodeDirectory hashes and permanent revocation (A-011, A-015, A-017, T-054). docs/provider/cli-reference.md (patch hunk near line 334) documents that after local HTTP admission closes during drain, new POSTs get HTTP 503 with an OpenAI-style error and the usual CORS header. Health reads and OPTIONS preflights stay available. This describes existing drain behavior and adds no new surface. I found no change to TB-002, TB-011, A-016 or T-053 and no new security regression. Later passes should check that the native Bonsai/MTP sidecar code (not in this batch) validates sidecar integrity and that the drain 503 matches the implementation. Neither can be verified from these docs.
